title: Q2: Frozen-controller retention and one-factor robustness
hypothesis: JOINT's state-conditioned residual compensates modest contact changes, keeping six-second sustained success within five percentage points of nominal under a 20% friction reduction.

prediction.against: Frozen config/pen_spin/r121_joint_finalist at nominal friction on the same fresh confirmation manifests
prediction.rationale: Primary contrast is JOINT at 0.8x friction minus nominal JOINT, with all other settings unchanged and the original six-second sustained-success endpoint. Predict a difference above -0.05: this permits modest degradation without calling it improvement. Support requires the paired 95% interval lower bound above -0.05; an upper bound below -0.05 refutes it; otherwise it is inconclusive. The margin preserves approximately 94% of archived nominal success. Use 1,280 paired cases, approximately the supplied worst-discordance sizing for this margin, rather than underpowering the primary contrast.

Update config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml with a frozen 12-condition OFAT panel: nominal 6 seconds; nominal dynamics at 12 and 30 seconds; six-second mass multipliers 0.8 and 1.2; friction multipliers 0.8 and 1.2 applied to both static and dynamic coefficients; radius multipliers 0.9 and 1.1; capsule-height/length multipliers 0.9 and 1.1; and reset-vector multiplier 1.5. In frozen_robustness.py, the six-second sustained success in every cell is: no termination before step 359 and the per-step predicate true on recorded steps 299..358 (identical to cases.sustained on a nominal 359-step trace). The primary six-second cells are scored by the unchanged evaluator; the 12 s and 30 s cells use exactly those step indices of their longer trace, and a nominal-prefix consistency check compares that prefix score with the 6 s cell on the same manifests. Longer-horizon cells run 720 or 1,800 steps with time-out auto-reset disabled until the declared horizon, with no time-constant rescaling and no additional recovery decision. Label longer-horizon endpoints separately. In frozen_robustness.py, freeze the primary analysis and secondary comparison list before outcomes. Report paired t intervals and manifest-clustered sensitivity intervals. Report every controller-condition cell; apply Holm correction across all predeclared non-primary tests, including condition shifts and comparisons against JOINT. Treat spin-distribution plots as descriptive. Non-inferiority, ties and intervals containing zero never establish an improvement; this study performs no promotion.

result.notes: 204 cells (4 controllers x 12 conditions x 4 manifests, plus JOINT nominal and 0.8x friction on 6 more), all complete, no rerun, 84 of 240 minutes, 12,558,093 scored transitions of 13,086,720 scheduled, no model calls, no fitting. Preflight (no rollout) read every condition back from the simulator: mass, both friction coefficients, capsule radius and length, horizon; all 12 passed, and every outcome cell re-checked its own physical record. PRIMARY: JOINT at 0.8x friction minus nominal JOINT on 1,280 pairs: -0.015, 95% interval [-0.035, +0.005] (manifest-clustered [-0.026, -0.004]); lower bound above -0.05, so SUPPORTED as non-inferiority at the registered margin (966 vs 985 successes; this is not an improvement and the clustered interval excludes zero on the negative side). Horizons: nothing is lost with time. JOINT's terminal success is 0.775 at 12 s and 0.781 at 30 s against 0.766 on the first six seconds of the same runs; in the 30 s cells all 24 drops occur in the first four seconds and per-second window success stays at 0.78 from second 6 to 30. Same for the transplant (0.807 / 0.811), D-072 (0.441 / 0.443) and PPO (0.994). One-factor physical shifts (512 pairs each, about +/-0.04 resolution): JOINT stays within -0.023 to +0.041 of nominal for mass, friction, radius and length; none is Holm-significant. The transplant is within -0.059 to -0.012 (radius 1.1x -0.059 [-0.096, -0.021], Holm p 0.12). D-072 loses 0.074 at radius 1.1x (Holm-significant). The expanded reset distribution (1.5x) is the real weakness: JOINT -0.281 [-0.331, -0.232] (0.770 -> 0.486), transplant -0.322, D-072 -0.141, PPO -0.125 (0.994 -> 0.869); JOINT's failures there shift to early drops (67 of 512) and off-centre (47). JOINT still beats D-072 there by 0.189. PPO competence control: 0.994 nominal and 0.99+ on mass, friction and radius, but 0.887 at 0.9x length (49 near-miss failures of 512) and 0.869 at 1.5x resets. Transplant minus JOINT is within +/-0.035 in all 12 conditions, none significant. Deviations: (1) the agreed per-cell re-capture trigger counts are UNAVAILABLE: evaluation cells do not record them (the driver first wrote zeros from a missing key; the local summary and the code now say unavailable); only the frozen decision steps (JOINT 149, transplant 149) are known, so no recovery-timing statement is made. (2) Nominal-prefix consistency is not exact for the module controllers: 1-2 of 512 cases differ between a longer run's first six seconds and the six-second cell (D-072 and PPO agree on all 512). (3) JOINT's nominal and 0.8x friction rows of the table pool ten manifests (1,280 cases); every other row is four manifests (512). (4) Friction is the pen material's coefficients; contact friction is PhysX's combination with the hand's material. Limits: one-factor only, frozen controllers of one lineage, secondary cells underpowered for a 0.05 margin.

verdicts.reasoning: By the frozen rule: JOINT at 0.8x friction minus nominal JOINT is -0.015 [-0.035, +0.005] over 1,280 pairs; the lower bound is above the -0.05 margin, so the non-inferiority prediction is supported (not an improvement; the manifest-clustered interval [-0.026, -0.004] suggests a small real loss inside the margin). Beyond the primary: no retention loss to 30 s (terminal success 0.781 vs 0.766 on the first six seconds; no drop after second 4), mass / friction / radius / length shifts leave JOINT within about +/-0.04 with nothing Holm-significant, but a 1.5x reset distribution costs JOINT -0.281 [-0.331, -0.232] and the transplant -0.322, more than it costs D-072 (-0.141) or PPO (-0.125). The hypothesis's mechanism (the residual compensating contact changes) is not tested: the transplant, with the untouched R-106 residual, is as robust as JOINT.
verdicts.next_experiment: The robustness gap is capture from wider resets, not dynamics or retention. That is a training-distribution question (propose separately, never retune on this panel). Proceed to Q3's archive-only diagnosis of recovery hand-back on JOINT/transplant traces, noting that evaluation cells do not record trigger events.

verdicts.reasoning: The named nominal JOINT control was measured: reduced friction produced 966 successes versus 985 nominal successes across 1,280 pairs, giving paired_success_difference = -0.01484375 with a 95% interval of [-0.03499434, 0.00530684] [logs/pen_spin/r129_frozen_robustness/summary.json]. The interval's lower bound exceeds the registered -0.05 margin, satisfying the support rule; the manifest-clustered interval [-0.02584911, -0.00383839] also remains above that margin [logs/pen_spin/r129_frozen_robustness/summary.json]. This supports non-inferiority, not improvement or residual-specific compensation: the primary interval includes zero, and the comparison does not isolate the residual's contribution [logs/pen_spin/r129_frozen_robustness/summary.json]. Robustness is not general across the panel: expanded resets reduce JOINT success by 0.28125, with interval [-0.33066, -0.23184] and a Holm-significant result [logs/pen_spin/r129_frozen_robustness/summary.json]. Missing recovery-trigger counts and imperfect nominal-prefix agreement limit recovery attribution and longer-horizon interpretation, without changing the registered primary contrast [logs/pen_spin/r129_frozen_robustness/summary.json].
verdicts.next_experiment: Audit archived JOINT spin/centre traces descriptively around the frozen recovery hand-back before deciding whether a state-dependent transition study is justified, reusing scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml with 0 simulator episodes and 0 LLM calls.

advisor.reasoning: Q1 is complete, making frozen-controller robustness the next priority; this protocol preserves the six-second endpoint while separately measuring longer-horizon retention without fitting. Its weakest point is mechanistic attribution: robustness of JOINT would not establish that its residual specifically compensates contact changes. The finite ceiling of 26,112 episodes, 240 minutes and zero controller-generation LLM calls is justified by the paired primary contrast and shared robustness panel. The registered prediction is an increase in paired_success_difference above -0.05 for JOINT at 0.8x friction versus nominal JOINT on identical fresh cases; it is falsified if the paired 95% interval lies entirely below -0.05, with inconclusive intervals and non-inferiority never counted as improvement.
